assumptions: The mandate and registry conditions stated in the supplied evidence remain applicable.
A meaningful subset of storage SMEs lacks an adequate incumbent solution.
The founder can use contractors for legal and standards-conformance work within the stated capital.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Paid readiness pilots converting into multi-year hosting agreements, measured onboarding hours and margins, plus successful registry interoperability using customer-authorized product data.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: A near-term mandatory battery passport creates a real implementation gap for smaller operators that lack enterprise PLM capability.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: The legal obligation and launch risk support meaningful pain, but reachable operators' willingness to outsource at the proposed prices is unvalidated.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Prepaid implementation and recurring lifecycle hosting could produce sound cash conversion, but 80-300 onboarding hours, enterprise CAC, and uncertain support burden constrain operating leverage.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Storage assemblers and importers form a coherent beachhead, although the number of reachable small operators and market concentration are unknown.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: A localized connector may win early accounts, but PLM, ERP, certification, and traceability incumbents can bundle the capability and already own integrations.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: Connectors and compliance workflows could extend across battery categories, suppliers, lifecycle updates, and adjacent product-passport regimes.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Accumulated mappings and field-quality benchmarks can compound, but customer data rights are nonexclusive and the proposed operator remains replaceable.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: A focused, lower-complexity service may beat enterprise suites for SMEs, but no demonstrated improvement in cost, speed, or compliance quality is supplied.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Registry testing is live and the February 2027 mandate creates an unusually strong, time-bounded buying catalyst.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Testing labs, renewable installers, and associations are plausible channels, but no customer relationship, referral commitment, or repeatable acquisition evidence exists.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The technical work fits the founder, but evolving rules, security obligations, manufacturer-data access, and potentially large implementations challenge part-time execution.

highest_value_structural_change: Secure a channel partnership with a battery testing or certification organization that supplies repeatable leads and embeds the service into mandatory conformity workflows.
main_structural_strength: A hard regulatory deadline supports a paid implementation wedge that can convert into recurring lifecycle-record revenue.
primary_score_limiter: The business does not yet control customer data rights or distribution and faces readily bundling incumbents.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Large manufacturers may build internally or use established PLM vendors, while detailed implementation requirements continued changing in 2026.
